title: Momentum and its conservation; Moments and static equilibrium; Systems and centre of mass
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D09-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D09-2#t3 term and clue written for the game; D09-2#t1 term and clue written for the game; D09-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D07-1#N.2, D08-1#N.2, D09-1#N.2, D09-2#N.3, D07-1#N.5, D08-1#N.5a, D09-1#N.7, D09-2#N.5, D09-1#N.16a, D09-2#N.7.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Momentum
items.clue: Vector equal to mass × velocity, measured in kg m s⁻¹.

items.label: Kinetic energy
items.clue: Quantity equal to p²/2m, which falls when two gliders stick together.

items.label: Elastic collision
items.clue: Type of impact in which the total of all the mv²/2 values is unchanged.

items.label: Newton's third law
items.clue: Reason two colliding bodies push each other with equal and opposite forces.

questions.stem: A cylindrical rod is made of a 0.50 m aluminium section joined end to end to a 0.50 m steel section of the same diameter. Each section is uniform, and the steel section has the greater mass. How does the location of the rod's centre of mass compare with the rod's midpoint?

options.text: It is at the midpoint, since the rod's shape is symmetric about that point.
It is on the aluminium side of the midpoint, nearer the lighter section.
It is at the centre of the steel section, the more massive part.
It lies between the midpoint and the centre of the steel section.

questions.stem: A mechanic pulls with a 20 N force on the end of a tool handle, 0.25 m from the centre of a nut. The force is in the plane of the handle's turn, but at 30° to the handle instead of at 90°. What is the turning effect of the force about the centre of the nut?

options.text: 5.0 N m
4.3 N m
80 N m
2.5 N m

questions.explanation: Perpendicular distance = 0.25 × sin 30° = 0.125 m, so the turning effect = 20 × 0.125 = 2.5 N m.

questions.stem: A cricket ball of mass m moving horizontally with speed v is struck by a bat. It leaves the bat moving horizontally with speed 3v/2 in the opposite direction. Taking the ball's initial direction of motion as positive, what is the change in the ball's momentum?

A 0.50 kg trolley moving at 5.0 m s⁻¹ collides with a 3.0 kg trolley at rest on a level track with negligible friction. After the collision, the 0.50 kg trolley moves backwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹ and the 3.0 kg trolley moves forwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹. How much of the system's kinetic energy is transformed into other forms of energy?
A rectangular wooden sign hangs from a single hook through a hole at the middle of its top edge. A heavy metal letter is fixed near the sign's left end. How does the sign hang at rest?

options.text: Level, because the hook is at the middle of the top edge.
Tilted, left end lower, with its centre of gravity directly below the hook.
Tilted, left end lower, until the metal letter is directly below the hook.
Tilted, right end lower, to balance the heavy letter.

questions.explanation: At rest the weight has no moment about the hook, so its line of action passes through the hook. The sign turns until its centre of gravity, shifted left by the letter, is vertically below the hook.

questions.stem: A uniform beam of length 5.0 m and weight 400 N rests horizontally on two supports, one at each end, P and Q. A person of weight 600 N stands on the beam 1.0 m from Q. What is the upward force from support P?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about Q: F_P × 5.0 = 400 × 2.5 + 600 × 1.0 = 1600 N m, so F_P = 320 N.

questions.stem: Two blocks, of masses 1.0 kg and 4.0 kg, are held at rest on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with a compressed spring between them. When they are released, the 1.0 kg block moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the 4.0 kg block is correct?

options.text: It moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 0.50 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 8.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It stays at rest, as the total momentum must stay zero.

questions.explanation: Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: 4.0 × v = 1.0 × 2.0, so v = 0.50 m s⁻¹, opposite to the 1.0 kg block.

questions.stem: An object of mass 4m at rest on a frictionless horizontal surface explodes into three pieces that slide along the surface. Immediately after the explosion, a piece of mass m moves at speed v in the +x-direction and a piece of mass 2m moves at speed 2v in the +y-direction. What is the speed of the third piece, of mass m?

options.text: 5v

questions.stem: A person of mass 60 kg stands in a rowing boat of mass 120 kg. Both are at rest, and water resistance is negligible. The person jumps horizontally from the boat onto a jetty, leaving at 1.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the boat immediately afterwards is correct?

options.text: It moves away from the jetty at 1.0 m s⁻¹, as the forces on the person and the boat are equal and opposite.
It stays at rest, as the person pushes off towards the jetty and not against the boat.
It moves away at 0.50 m s⁻¹, with the same kinetic energy as the person.
It moves away at 0.50 m s⁻¹, with momentum equal and opposite to the person's.

questions.stem: A 2.0 kg trolley moving at 3.0 m s⁻¹ collides head-on with a 1.0 kg trolley at rest on a level, frictionless track. Afterwards the 2.0 kg trolley moves on in the same direction at 1.0 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of the 1.0 kg trolley, and what type of collision is this?

options.text: 4.0 m s⁻¹ forwards; elastic, as the total kinetic energy is 9.0 J before and after.
4.0 m s⁻¹ forwards; inelastic, as the 2.0 kg trolley lost kinetic energy.
2.0 m s⁻¹ forwards; inelastic, as kinetic energy falls from 9.0 J to 3.0 J.
8.0 m s⁻¹ forwards; impossible, as kinetic energy would rise to 33 J.
